chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to bury his hair in his tent in Mina, and he said: 'They used to prefer that.' He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked that the hair be taken out of Mina, and he said: Whoever takes it out must return it.'

key_terms.مِنًى: A sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims perform specific rituals

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on disposing of hair cut during Hajj in Mina according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the jurisprudential nuance between the Sunnah of burying hair in Mina, as practiced by Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), and the stricter precautionary view of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding its removal. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the sanctity of the Hajj sites by ensuring that physical remnants of the pilgrim do not leave the sacred precincts, thereby preserving the ritual completeness of the sacrifice.
